workload.prompt_source: DMS data-manifest validation stream (identical token slice across arms)
workload.route_shape: one resident C1 session per arm, bulk prefill, greedy per-step decode

finding: After the DMS speed campaign, both DMS codecs decode faster than the dense route at 16K context on the W7900: dense BF16 45.55 ms/step, DMS BF16 37.92 (-16.7%), DMS INT8 38.29 (-15.9%) - with DMS's capacity advantage intact (the compact payload). Cumulative: BF16 55.39 -> 37.92 (1.46x) and INT8 91.79 -> 38.29 (2.40x). The wins: wave-group6 split-K producer enabled on gfx1100 (bf16), chunked keep-scan append (int8), wave-grouped GQA int8 producer, staging-upload hoist, in-place finalize. Attention kernels now run near their bandwidth rooflines (bf16 0.344 -> 0.079 ms, int8 0.723 -> 0.077 ms at live 8192). Greedy tokens identical to the pre-campaign baselines per codec throughout.
caveats: Single session, one prompt, one process per arm; diagnostics only - not a retained benchmark and no production performance claim.
Cross-GPU comparisons (e.g. against the XTX lane) require a same-host protocol measuring both.
DMS numerics differ from dense by design (eviction + int8 codec); quality gates are the capacity campaign's scope, not this probe's.
